title: Exact augmented free simplex module complex at each component
statement: Let $m\ge 0$ and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. For an ordinary $\Lambda$-module $M$, form the augmented chain complex indexed by the simplex category [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] whose degree-$p$ term is $C_p(m,M)=\bigoplus_{\alpha:[p]\to[m]}M$, whose differential is the alternating sum of the maps carrying the $\alpha$ summand to the $\alpha\delta_i$ summand, and whose augmentation $C_0(m,M)\to M$ folds all summands by the identity. Then this augmented complex $\cdots\to C_2(m,M)\to C_1(m,M)\to C_0(m,M)\to M\to0$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 0D7C (lemma-simplicial-resolution-augmentation-modules), componentwise complex and its vertex-zero extra-degeneracy contraction; compare Tag 0D72 for the direct-sum component formula.

proof.text: Write $e_\alpha(x)$ for $x\in M$ in the summand indexed by $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, and put $C_{-1}=M$ and $d_0=\epsilon$; for $p\ge1$ write $d_p e_\alpha(x)=\sum_{i=0}^p(-1)^i e_{\alpha\delta_i}(x)$. The face injections of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] delete entries of the nondecreasing tuple $(\alpha(0),\ldots,\alpha(p))$. For $p\ge2$, each double deletion with original positions $i<j$ occurs in $d_{p-1}d_p$ twice: deleting $j$ then $i$ has sign $(-1)^{j+i}$, and deleting $i$ then position $j-1$ has sign $(-1)^{i+j-1}$. The terms cancel, even when tuples coincide. Also $\epsilon d_1e_\alpha(x)=x-x=0$. Thus these maps form the asserted augmented complex.

source.place: Tag 0D7C (lemma-simplicial-resolution-augmentation-modules), last sentence, via Tag 0D78 (lemma-simplicial-resolution-augmentation), component simplex complex; explicit elementary contraction supplied here.

proof.text: For $p\ge0$ define $\widehat\alpha:[p+1]\to[m]$ by $\widehat\alpha(0)=0$ and $\widehat\alpha(j+1)=\alpha(j)$. It is nondecreasing since $0\le\alpha(0)$ and $\alpha$ is nondecreasing; the vertex $0$ exists because $m\ge0$. Define $h_p:C_p\to C_{p+1}$ by $h_pe_\alpha(x)=e_{\widehat\alpha}(x)$ and $h_{-1}:M\to C_0$ by $h_{-1}(x)=e_{(0)}(x)$. Each formula is linear on each summand and sends a finitely supported sum to a finitely supported sum, so it defines a $\Lambda$-linear map. In particular $\epsilon h_{-1}=\mathrm{id}_M$.

source.place: Tag 0D7C (lemma-simplicial-resolution-augmentation-modules), last sentence, via Tag 0D78 (lemma-simplicial-resolution-augmentation), component simplex complex; explicit elementary contraction supplied here.

proof.text: For $p\ge1$, deleting position $0$ of $\widehat\alpha$ gives $\alpha$, and deleting position $i+1$ gives $\widehat{\alpha\delta_i}$. Consequently $d_{p+1}h_pe_\alpha(x)=e_\alpha(x)+\sum_{i=0}^p(-1)^{i+1}e_{\widehat{\alpha\delta_i}}(x)=e_\alpha(x)-h_{p-1}d_pe_\alpha(x)$. For $p=0$, the boundary of the edge $(0,\alpha(0))$ gives $d_1h_0e_\alpha(x)=e_\alpha(x)-e_{(0)}(x)=e_\alpha(x)-h_{-1}\epsilon e_\alpha(x)$. Linearity extends these equalities to all elements. Thus $d_{p+1}h_p+h_{p-1}d_p=\mathrm{id}_{C_p}$ in every degree $p\ge0$, with $d_0=\epsilon$.

source.place: Tag 0D7C (lemma-simplicial-resolution-augmentation-modules), last sentence, via Tag 0D78 (lemma-simplicial-resolution-augmentation), component simplex complex; explicit elementary contraction supplied here.

proof.text: If $z\in C_p$ and $d_pz=0$ ($p\ge0$, taking $d_0=\epsilon$), the identity in step 3 gives $z=d_{p+1}(h_pz)$. Hence $\ker d_p\subseteq\operatorname{im}d_{p+1}$; step 1 gives the reverse inclusion. At $M$, every $x$ equals $\epsilon h_{-1}(x)$ by step 2, so the augmentation is surjective. The map $M\to0$ has kernel $M$, and exactness at the final zero is automatic. This proves exactness at every term, with no flatness, freeness or finiteness condition on $M$.
